title: Generate a labelled set of stylised pictures and measure how many faces PixlStash finds today
body: Make the test pictures with an image generator rather than collecting them: around 200 pictures across styles such as flat cartoon, 3D-rendered cartoon, clay figures (stop-motion style characters like the owner's example, Barry the Gnome), manga and anime, plus about 100 photographic pictures for comparison. Writing the prompts ourselves means each style can be covered evenly, with a known number of characters in each picture, and the set can be regenerated or extended later. A box is then drawn by hand around every face, and PixlStash's current face finder (the InsightFace SCRFD-10G detector at its present settings: the picture shrunk to 512 px on its long side, the detector working at 256 px, confidence cut-off 0.25) is run over all of them. Nothing is improved by this idea itself; it exists because no measurement of face detection quality exists in the project, so every other idea has nothing to be judged against. It reports recall (the share of hand-boxed faces the detector found, counting a found box as a match when it overlaps the hand box by at least half) and false finds per picture, separately for each style and for photos. The result counts if it gives stable numbers per style that the other ideas can be compared with; it would also confirm or refute the owner's impression, for example by showing clay-figure recall at 20% against 95% for photos.
